          Triple Threat: Can London City Lionesses' Attacking Trio Make WSL History?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 15, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Emily Millen / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Alexia Putellas, Kadidiatou Diani and Daniëlle van de Donk have hit the ground running in London City Lionesses’ first five WSL matches of 2026-27. But how does their goal and assist output compare with the league’s most prolific attacking trios across history?

London City Lionesses’ 6-1 demolition of Tottenham last time out was more than a statement victory. It was a glimpse of what the club could become: an ambitious disruptor capable of unsettling the WSL’s established order.

Eder Maestre’s side did not simply outscore Spurs, but they repeatedly turned possession into dangerous attacks. The result was London City’s largest ever WSL victory, with the visitors recording 5.99 expected goals (xG) – the highest total by an away team in the competition since Opta’s records began in 2017-18.

They also scored six times from just 10 shots on target, the fewest by a team scoring 6+ goals in a WSL game since Chelsea’s 6-0 victory over Man Utd in May 2024 (nine shots on target), highlighting both the quality of their chances and their clinical finishing.

At the heart of the performance was the attacking trio of Alexia Putellas, Kadidiatou Diani and Daniëlle van de Donk. Putellas scored twice, Diani added two goals and an assist, while Van de Donk scored once and provided two assists. Between them, they contributed eight goal involvements in a performance that exposed the threat of London City’s revamped attack.
Just as striking was the fluidity between the three.

Diani held the right flank, Van de Donk drifted in from the left channel to attack the penalty area, and Putellas moved across the pitch to link play and create opportunities. Their roles were complementary giving Spurs few straightforward defensive tasks.

Although their stats stood out in the win over Spurs, in truth, the trio have displayed that form across the whole campaign. Over the first five WSL matchdays, the three players have registered 14 goal involvements in total: five for Van de Donk, five for Diani and four for Putellas. Their output has helped London City collect 12 points from a possible 15 and climb to third in the table before the international break.

That points tally is significant in its own right. No team to have collected at least 12 points after the opening five matches has finished below fifth in WSL history. For a club looking to build on last season’s sixth-place finish, the early signs suggest another step forward, with their attacking firepower central to the progress.

Their influence is clearest in the penalty area. Van de Donk leads London City with 30 touches in the opposition box, followed by Putellas (24) and Diani (19). The figures reflect their complementary roles, but also a shared strength: all three are consistently finding dangerous positions and putting themselves in a place to influence the outcome.

But how does this trio compare with the most prolific attacking combinations in WSL history? And if Putellas, Diani and Van de Donk can sustain anything close to their current rate of production, could they join the competition’s greatest ever trios?
Fourteen goal involvements in five matches is an impressive return. It's also a useful benchmark against some of the league’s most memorable attacking units.
Across WSL history, these are the standout combinations across total goal involvements to provide a measure of the challenge ahead:

The Chelsea trio of Sam Kerr, Fran Kirby and Bethany England set a formidable benchmark in 2020-21. Kerr and Kirby each recorded 28 non-penalty goal involvements, while England added 15 herself, taking their combined total to 71 – the highest of any three-player attacking combination in our comparison.

Arsenal’s holy trinity of Vivianne Miedema, Beth Mead and Van de Donk amassed 67 in 2018-19, while Man City’s Khadija Shaw, Chloe Kelly and Lauren Hemp combined for 53 in 2022-23. These are among the most well-known attacking combinations of the WSL era, offering a useful benchmark for London City’s new-look forward line.
The early-season numbers make for an intriguing comparison.

Across their first five matchdays, Chelsea’s 2020-21 trio and Man City’s 2022-23 combination each recorded 13 goal involvements. Arsenal’s three in 2018-19, however, had already amassed 25 – a reminder that blistering starts can take different paths over the course of a season.
The early return of the London City trio therefore offers a reason for optimism, not a reliable prediction of what is to come.

The expanded 14-team WSL season comprises 26 league matches. If the trio maintain their current average of 2.8 involvements per match, a simple extrapolation would give them 72.8 goal involvements across the campaign, enough to edge the Chelsea benchmark in this comparison.

But, the more meaningful question is whether London City can sustain enough of their current production to remain in the conversation as the season develops; their total 15 goals is only bettered by Tottenham and City on 16.
